record.paper_title: Multiplier sequences, classes of generalized Bessel functions and open problems
record.original_question: For every real number s>0, does there exist an integer m>=1 such that the entire function sum_{k>=0} k^s x^k/(k!)^m belongs to L-P+? Here L-P+ denotes the subclass of the Laguerre-Polya class consisting of real entire functions whose Taylor coefficients are all nonnegative.

evidence.quote: Problem 40. Is it true that for every s in R^+, there exists an m in N, such that sum_{k=0}^infinity k^s x^k/(k!)^m belongs to L - P+.
If gamma_k >= 0 for k = 0, 1, 2, ..., we write phi in L - P+.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^{+}$ denote the subclass of the Laguerre–Pólya class consisting of real entire functions $\varphi(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\gamma_k x^k$ all of whose Taylor coefficients satisfy $\gamma_k\ge 0$ and which can be expressed as a (possibly finite) locally uniform limit of polynomials having only real zeros. Equivalently, $\varphi\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^{+}$ if and only if $\varphi$ has the Hadamard factorization
$$\varphi(x)=c\,x^{n}e^{\alpha x}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\left(1+\tfrac{x}{x_k}\right),$$
where $c\ge 0$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, $\alpha\ge 0$, $x_k>0$, and $\sum 1/x_k<\infty$.

For each real number $s>0$, consider the entire function
$$F_{s,m}(x)\;=\;\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{k^{s}}{(k!)^{m}}\,x^{k}, \qquad m\in\mathbb{N}.$$

Prove or disprove: for every real $s>0$ there exists an integer $m\ge 1$ such that $F_{s,m}\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^{+}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in the literature on multiplier sequences and generalized Bessel-type functions (a paper that lists numerous conjectures and open problems concerning the Laguerre–Pólya class). A web search did not turn up any subsequent publication resolving the existence-of-$m$ question for arbitrary $s>0$; related work treats specific Fox–Wright/Bessel-type families but does not settle this problem.

status_evidence.claim: The problem appears in a collection of open problems on multiplier sequences and Laguerre–Pólya class membership.

status_evidence.title: The Fox–Wright functions and Laguerre multiplier sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of Fox–Wright type entire functions and their membership in the Laguerre–Pólya class, related to but not resolving the k^s/(k!)^m question.
status_evidence.claim: Related follow-up work addresses analogous families but does not resolve the existence of m for every s>0.
